content: Shared global memory and fact graph contain no prior results. Use barycentric coordinates. Put r=BD/DC, s=CE/EA, t=AF/FB. Then D=(B+rC)/(1+r), E=(sA+C)/(1+s), F=(A+tB)/(1+t). If a common point P has barycentric coordinates (alpha,beta,gamma), incidence with AD, BE, CF respectively yields gamma=r beta, alpha=s gamma, beta=t alpha; nonzero coordinates follow because the common point cannot equal a vertex lying off the other cevian. Hence rst=1. Conversely if rst=1, P=(rs A+B+r C)/(rs+1+r) lies on all three cevians, using t=1/(rs).
